newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi prince to buy Paris's famed Hotel George V.
newsitem.headline: Saudi prince to buy Paris's famed Hotel George V.

text.p: Saudi billionaire Prince al-Waleed bin Talal said on Wednesday he would buy the luxury Hotel George V in Paris -- "the best hotel in the world" -- from Britain's Granada Group Plc for $172 million.
A statement from the prince's office in Riyadh said the transaction would be completed after a meeting of the Workers Committee of the Hotel George V, called for Wednesday.

Speaking by telephone from Riyadh, the prince told Reuters the 258-room hotel in the heart of Paris would undergo a "major renovation programme" starting sometime next year. He would not say how much he would spend on the upgrade.
The Granada sale is the second in a planned disposal of 17 luxury Exclusive hotels acquired as part of its January takeover of hotel and catering empire Forte, but now seen as non-core.
Granada had put the hotel's book value at 92 million sterling -- 12 million sterling less than what Prince al-Waleed paid.

Asked why he chose this hotel for his portfolio -- which ranges from stakes in banks, to retailers and theme parks -- the entrepreneurial grandson of Saudi Arabia's founder, King Abdul-Aziz al-Saud, said "because it is the best hotel in the world, that's my point of view".
"The Hotel George V is one of the most famous hotels in Europe and we believe it has the potential to become one of the most successful hotels in the world," he said.
Industry sources said the prince had snatched the deal from the Sultan of Brunei, rated the world's richest man, and his brother, at the last moment.
Asked if he was buying the 68-year-old favourite of celebrities and dignitaries on his own, Prince al-Waleed said: "Oh yes, alone. No one else at all."
The prince has built a multi-billion dollar business empire with interests in construction, real estate, banking, travel, broadcast media, supermarkets and other sectors.

He heads the United Saudi Commercial Bank and has made substantial investments in Citicorp, Euro Disney SCA which owns a theme park near Paris, Canary Wharf in London's Docklands, U.S. upmarket retail group Saks Fifth Avenue and the Plaza Hotel in New York.
His portfolio also includes stakes in the Four Seasons and Fairmont Hotel chains. Recently he set up Kingdom Entertainment with U.S. popstar Michael Jackson.
Prince al-Waleed said he had been planning to purchase Hotel George V "since the Forte era" but negotiations had taken "some time".
